**Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Henrik Larsson -** Henrik leads Tessera, an Australian managed-cloud and multi-tenant SaaS provider founded in 2011 and now serving more than 600 clients from offices in Perth, Sydney and Malaga. He sets the company's strategic direction against hyperscale competition and the realities of running roughly 210 staff. Following TSR-INC-2025-031 - the February 2025 breach that exposed about 14,000 tenant records - the board mandated an ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification-readiness programme, which Henrik now sponsors. He has also commissioned an independent AI-readiness assessment, weighing genuine opportunity against the well-documented failure rate of AI initiatives. Tessera has no formal AI strategy, budget or executive sponsor yet, and Henrik is candid about the gap between ambition and capability.

**Interview Focus: CEO Henrik Larsson**
Students should probe Tessera's strategic position and Henrik's priorities after the breach. Useful lines of questioning: why the board responded to TSR-INC-2025-031 with an ISO 27001:2022 certification mandate rather than a narrower fix; how he frames the trade-off between growth and security maturity; the rationale and timing of the AI-readiness assessment; how he manages board and stakeholder expectations while the company still lacks a formal AI strategy, budget or sponsor; and how he reads the competitive landscape against the hyperscalers.
